title: Roundtrip All-Pairs Shortest Paths in Directed Graphs: Invariant Preservation and Complexity Analysis in Chronos-Interpreter
topic: Roundtrip All-Pairs Shortest Paths in Directed Graphs
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We study the roundtrip all-pairs shortest-path (APSP) problem on directed weighted graphs, where the roundtrip distance from vertex $i$ to $j$ and back to $i$ is required. The core algorithm is a Floyd--Warshall implementation that maintains the optimal-substructure invariant across all intermediate-vertex sets, followed by a linear-time aggregation to obtain the roundtrip matrix. We formally prove that the algorithm preserves the invariant that after processing the first $k$ vertices, every entry $\text{dist}[i][j]$ equals the shortest path from $i$ to $j$ using only intermediate vertices in $\{0,\dots,k\}$. The asymptotic cost is $O(|V|^{3})$ for APSP and $O(|V|^{2})$ for the roundtrip matrix, with a static-analysis-derived structural complexity of 186 SLOC and 10 function blocks. No empirical timing data are reported; all claims are supported by formal proofs and AST inspection. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/Chronos-Interpreter-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261104_170122_roundtrip_all-pairs_shortest_p}
